paper_metadata.title: Time-domain-multiplexed Gaussian Boson sampling for graph problems in finance

experiments.description: Gaussian Boson Sampling (GBS) community-structure analysis for market anomaly screening on a synthetic financial transaction graph with four detected communities.

algorithm.variant: Gaussian Boson Sampling for dense-subgraph/community detection

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Transaction graph is converted to an adjacency matrix A; A is decomposed as A = U diag(lambda_i) U^T, with lambda_i mapped to squeezing parameters via tanh(r_i) = lambda_i. Output probabilities are used as a proxy for graph density.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Identify communities whose GBS sampling probabilities correlate with intrinsic graph density.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on fixed-size subgraphs; comparison against random-sampled subgraph density baseline.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic financial network with four distinct communities.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic graph where nodes represent bank accounts and edges represent transactions; four communities are visualized and evaluated.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Graph construction from transaction data; adjacency matrix computation.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Correlation of GBS probability with graph density; comparison to averages from 10,000 randomly sampled 4-node and 6-node subgraphs.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Convert transaction data to graph and adjacency matrix.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Rank/inspect sampled subgraphs by probability and compare with graph density.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports correlation between GBS probability and graph density, but no explicit accuracy/F1/AUC or runtime speedup is given.

experiments.description: GBS-based synthetic identity fraud detection via hierarchical dense-subgraph identification on a bipartite account-PII graph.

algorithm.variant: Gaussian Boson Sampling for dense-subgraph detection

problem_formulation.encoding_details: A bipartite graph connects account nodes to PII nodes (e.g., email or physical address); dense subgraphs are identified through GBS output probabilities.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Find the densest subgraphs corresponding to fraudulent collusion in a financial identity graph.

problem_instance.description: A 20-node subgraph containing hierarchical dense subgraphs selected from a larger financial fraud dataset.

dataset_specification.description: Original dataset described as a bipartite graph with 29,851 account nodes and 61,159 PII nodes; the paper evaluates a 20-node subgraph extracted from it.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Construct bipartite graph from account-PII associations; extract a 20-node illustrative subgraph.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Identify densest subgraphs of sizes 6, 8, and 10 and compare GBS probability with graph density.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Graph construction from account-PII relations; subgraph extraction.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select subgraphs with highest GBS probabilities as dense-subgraph candidates.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit classical baseline metric or runtime comparison is reported; only qualitative comparison to dense-subgraph methods is discussed.

experiments.description: GBS-based collusive stock manipulation detection via clique enumeration on a synthetic trading network.

algorithm.variant: Gaussian Boson Sampling for clique finding

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Nodes represent investors and edges represent highly correlated trading behavior; cliques are identified from high-probability Fock states corresponding to fully connected subgraphs.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Enumerate cliques in a trading network to detect coordinated market manipulation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on fixed-size subgraphs with si in {0,1} and total photon number equal to clique size.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic 20-node stock-market transaction graph with a largest detected 7-node clique.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic graph simulating manipulated stock market transactions; 20-node graph used for the clique-finding demonstration.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Construct transaction graph from correlated trading behaviors.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Compare GBS output probabilities for the top 50 states; identify clique states by highest probabilities.

implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Sort sampled states by probability and map them to clique candidates.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not report a classical clique-finding baseline result, only the GBS output distribution and identified clique counts.

experiments.description: GBS-based anti-money laundering detection via isomorphic subgraph matching on a synthetic banking transaction graph containing a 6-node cycle pattern.

algorithm.variant: Gaussian Boson Sampling for isomorphic subgraph matching

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Pattern graph and target graph are encoded into GBS; if the pattern graph has odd size or zero Hafnian, auxiliary nodes are added to both graphs and candidates must include all auxiliary nodes.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Match a known anomalous pattern graph to isomorphic subgraphs in a target transaction graph using Hafnian-based signatures.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Auxiliary-node augmentation and post-selection of subgraphs containing all auxiliary nodes.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic banking transaction dataset with a 20-node extracted subgraph containing a 6-node cycle; two isomorphic subgraphs are identified.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic banking transaction dataset generated with AMLSim; paper states nodes n in {8,16,32,64,128} x 10^3 in the source dataset and uses an 8,000-node dataset for the illustrative 20-node subgraph extraction.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Extract a 20-node subgraph containing a 6-node cycle from the larger AML dataset; compute Hafnian-scaled probabilistic signatures.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Pre-compute pattern signature, run GBS on target graph, and match Hafnian-based signatures to identify isomorphic subgraphs.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Add auxiliary nodes when needed; compute Hafnian-based signatures for the pattern graph.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Match Hafnian signatures against target-graph subgraphs and retain candidates containing all auxiliary nodes.

speedup_claims.caveats: No explicit classical subgraph-isomorphism runtime or accuracy baseline is reported in the paper excerpt.

experiments.description: Time-domain-multiplexed photonic circuit fitting experiment: optimize a hybrid TDM architecture to approximate a 20x20 unitary derived from a collusive stock manipulation graph, and then use the fitted circuit for clique-finding GBS sampling.

algorithm.variant: Spatial-temporal hybrid time-domain-multiplexed photonic circuit for GBS
algorithm.ansatz: Hybrid TDM circuit with spatial blocks (two-layer alternating MZI meshes) and temporal blocks (delay loops)
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Best fidelity across 8 rounds of batched optimization over 350 epochs; final result is the highest fidelity among 640 optimization instances.
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Randomly initialized circuit parameters for each optimization instance

problem_formulation.encoding_method: adjacency-matrix encoding via unitary fitting for GBS
problem_formulation.encoding_details: A 20x20 unitary matrix U derived from the adjacency matrix A of a collusive stock manipulation graph is embedded into a larger global unitary implemented by the TDM circuit.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize fidelity between the target unitary U and the fitted submatrix U_fit extracted from the global TDM circuit.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Sliding-window search over contiguous N x N sub-blocks of the unrolled global unitary to find the best embedding.

problem_instance.description: 20-node collusive stock manipulation graph used both for unitary fitting and clique-finding demonstration.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic 20-node graph representing collusive stock manipulation; used to derive the 20x20 target unitary and to test 6-node clique finding.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Adjacency matrix is converted to a target unitary via Takagi-Autonne decomposition; clique-finding uses 6-photon post-selection on 20 modes.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Report best fidelity versus timesteps and compare top-50 output-state probabilities between ideal spatial GBS and TDM GBS.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Takagi-Autonne decomposition; sliding-window search for best embedded submatrix; random initialization across 640 optimization runs.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Select highest-fidelity fitted unitary and identify clique states from high-probability outputs.

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: fidelity increases with timesteps and saturates; best fidelity 0.9908 at 10 timesteps

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic reduction in hardware complexity; O(sqrt(N)) width and O(sqrt(N)) depth
speedup_claims.baseline_method: spatial Clements architecture / universal spatial interferometer
speedup_claims.conditions: For the proposed non-universal spatial-temporal hybrid architecture targeting problem-specific unitary fitting
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a hardware-complexity claim, not a demonstrated runtime speedup on a finance benchmark. Universality is sacrificed for scalability.
The paper states performance degrades as modes decrease, but does not provide exact fidelities for the 1–3 mode cases in text.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(sqrt(N)) width and O(sqrt(N)) depth for the proposed hybrid architecture
